item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=Thought+Space+Explorer+blind+spot+navigation+large+language+models+reasoning+EACL+2026&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.18653/v1/2026.findings-eacl.191\", \"title\": [\"Blind Spot Navigation in Large Language Model Reasoning with Thought Space Explorer\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2026.findings-eacl.191\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/bigdata62323.2024.10825638\", \"title\": [\"Thought Space Explorer: Navigating and Expanding Thought Space for Large Language Model Reasoning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/bigdata62323.2024.10825638\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 12, 15]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.36227/techrxiv.175756693.33854887/v1\", \"title\": [\"Meta-of-Thought: Reasoning About Reasoning in Large Language Models\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Recent progress in reasoning with large language models (LLMs) has been driven by prompting strategies such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Tree-of-Thought (ToT), Graph-of-Thought (GoT), and Hypergraph-of-Thought (HoT). Each introduces a powerful but fixed paradigm, forcing practitioners to manually select how a model should reason. In contrast, humans adapt their reasoning style-choosing between linear deduction, branching exploration, or relational inference depending on the task. We introduce Meta-of-Thought (MoT), a unifying controller that enables LLMs to reason about reasoning. MoT dynamically selects the most appropriate paradigm-CoT for arithmetic, ToT for planning, GoT for relational queries, and HoT for multimodal or scientific reasoning-closing the gap between fixed strategies and adaptive human cognition. A minimal rule-based prototype using flan-t5-small shows that MoT improves flexibility and robustness compared to static prompting. We position MoT as a step toward metacognitive LLMs that not only generate thoughts, but also decide how to think, opening a path for the next generation of reasoning research.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.36227/techrxiv.175756693.33854887/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 9, 11]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.18653/v1/2026.findings-eacl.27\", \"title\": [\"The Price of Thought: A Multilingual Analysis of Reasoning, Performan…
